To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $12.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}p-\frac{1}{4}q=3 & |\,\times 12 \\ -4p-7q=4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4p-3q=36 \\ -4p-7q=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $4p$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-4p$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $p$-variable, and allows us to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{4p}-3q & =36 \\ -\cancel{4p}-7q & =4 \\ -10q & =40 \\ q & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $q=-4$ into the equation $-4p-7q=4$ to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-4p-7q & =4 \\ -4p-7\cdot (-4) & =4 \\ -4p+28 & =4 \\ -4p & =-24 \\ p & =6\end{aligned}
$$

q-216035.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{3}{2}y=-5 \\ -2x-y=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{3}{2}y=-5 & |\,\times 6 \\ -2x-y=-2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2x+9y=-30 \\ -2x-y=-2\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $2x$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-2x$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable, and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{2x}+9y & =-30 \\ -\cancel{2x}-y & =-2 \\ 8y & =-32 \\ y & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-y & =-2 \\ -2x-(-4) & =-2 \\ -2x+4 & =-2 \\ -2x & =-6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
